home_hero_pill: a single Rust binary · open source · GPL-2.0
home_hero_description: KROMA brings the indexer, the download engine, the VPN, the server and the player together under one self-hosted server. Direct-play, native HEVC, on the web, on mobile and on every television.
home_one_binary_lead: A typical setup bolts together half a dozen services: six configs, six things that break, never at the same time. KROMA replaces them with a single Rust server that starts in milliseconds and keeps no transcoding farm warm.
home_features_intro: Find, download, organize, stream. Every link of a self-hosted media library, written once and shared, with nothing to wire between them.
home_features_acquisition_body: Ask for a title: KROMA searches every one of your indexers, scores each release on resolution, codec, size, seeders and your keywords, grabs the best one, then imports and renames it Plex-style.
home_features_vpn_body: Paste a WireGuard config and all torrent traffic goes through a managed WireGuard→SOCKS5 bridge. A failed tunnel check pauses every download on the spot: no leak, no Gluetun to wire up.
home_features_indexers_body: A reimplemented Cardigann engine runs the tracker definitions from Jackett and Prowlarr, directly.
home_features_downloader_body: A librqbit BitTorrent client fetches releases directly, driven by KROMA. Transmission and qBittorrent stay supported.
home_features_player_body: Original files are streamed by byte range and decoded by the client. Video is never re-encoded.
home_features_ai_body: Recommendations and semantic search over local embeddings, subtitles generated by Whisper. On your machine, no cloud.
home_features_users_body: Accounts, profiles, PIN locks, WebAuthn passkeys, invitations and per-user permissions. Share without opening everything up.
home_features_stats_body: Downloads, library scans and playback pushed in real time over a WebSocket bus, to dashboards and clients.
home_direct_play_lead: KROMA streams the original files by byte range; each client decodes HEVC/H.265 itself, in 10-bit and HDR, in hardware on Samsung and LG televisions. No transcoding pipeline, no CPU farm to keep warm.
home_direct_play_exception: One exception: an audio-only HLS stream for browsers that cannot decode AC3/EAC3/DTS. The video is copied, only the audio is transcoded to stereo AAC.
home_direct_play_cpu_note: Nothing to re-encode: playback never wakes the processor. Your NAS stays free for everything else.
home_platforms_title: The same KROMA, on every screen
home_platforms_intro: The components and design tokens exist once, in a shared kit, and render natively, from the browser to the living room driven by a remote.
home_self_host_lead: Open source, under the GPL-2.0 license. No account to create, no subscription, no central service that could shut down. Your library and your activity never leave your network.
home_final_cta_heading: Take back control of your [media library].
home_final_cta_lead: One binary to launch, your hardware, your files. No subscription, no data leaking out.
download_hero_h1: Install KROMA on [every screen you own].
download_hero_lede: The model fits in one sentence: install the server once, then every client, TV, computer, phone, browser, points at it and remembers it.
download_hero_server_detail: Installed once, on a NAS, in Docker or on a Raspberry Pi.
download_hero_client_detail: Every screen asks for its address on startup.
download_server_step_intro: A single Rust server: on a NAS, in Docker, or built by hand. It serves the API, the web app and the video stream on port 4040 in direct-play: video is never transcoded.
download_server_docker_body: The image is *multi-architecture* (`linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`) : it runs just as well on x86 as on a Raspberry Pi 4/5 with a 64-bit OS. Save this file, then bring the stack up.
download_server_docker_media_body: `KROMA_MEDIA_DIRS` points at your media *inside* the container; mount the folder read-write if you use the built-in requests / downloads.
download_server_synology_body: The package is self-signed, not Synology-certified: you have to allow it once.
download_server_synology_step_1: *Package Center → Settings → Trust Level* : allow *Any publisher*.
download_server_synology_step_2: *Package Center → Manual Install*, pick the `.spk`, follow the wizard.
download_server_synology_step_3: Open KROMA; configure the media folders in its admin console.
download_server_cargo_body: A single Rust binary: build it yourself. SQLite and TLS are bundled; ffmpeg/ffprobe are still required for metadata and HLS audio.
download_apps_step_intro: Grab the right package from *GitHub Releases* (one `vX.Y.Z` tag carries every artifact). A single setup per device, developer mode or lifting quarantine, then the client asks for the server address on first launch.
download_family_tv_intro: Sideload from a computer on the same network. Developer mode is enabled once.
download_family_tv_samsung_body: The *Apps* panel, type `1 2 3 4 5`, turn it on and enter your computer's IP. The `.wgt` is already signed, no certificate required, just the Tizen Studio CLI.
download_family_tv_lg_body: Install the *Developer Mode* app (free LG account), enable *Dev Mode* then *Key Server*. The session lasts 50 h, extend it from the app.
download_family_tv_androidtv_body: Settings → About → *Android TV OS build* : tap 7 times, then enable network debugging. Without a computer, the *Downloader* app installs the `.apk` from a URL.
download_family_desktop_intro: Regular installers. The desktop apps update themselves from there on.
download_family_desktop_mac_body: Not notarized: on first launch, macOS calls it "damaged". Drag it into Applications, then lift the quarantine once (or Settings → Privacy → *Open anyway*).
download_family_desktop_win_body: Unsigned installer: "Windows protected your PC" → *More info* → *Run anyway*. Silent updates from there on.
download_family_desktop_linux_body: mpv is bundled (the `kroma-mpv` sidecar drives hardware decoding), nothing to install.
download_family_desktop_steamdeck_step_1: Copy `KROMA_*.AppImage` onto the Deck and `chmod +x` (Desktop Mode).
download_family_desktop_steamdeck_step_2: *Steam → Add a Non-Steam Game → Browse*, then pick the AppImage.
download_family_desktop_steamdeck_step_3: Launch in Game Mode, set the controller layout to *Gamepad* (D-pad = focus, A = OK, B = back).
download_family_mobile_intro: The phone apps are being finished, distributed through the test channels.
download_family_mobile_ios_body: Join the iOS beta through TestFlight.
download_family_nas_intro: Where the server already lives, there is usually nothing more to install.
download_family_nas_web_body: The server serves the web app itself. Open its address in any browser, or let mDNS discovery find it on the network.
download_family_nas_synology_body: The best route on a NAS: add KROMA as a *package source* in Package Center. The server installs, then updates itself, without re-downloading a `.spk` for every release.
download_family_nas_synology_step_2: Paste the source URL below, then confirm the *"Any publisher"* trust level (the package is self-signed).
download_family_nas_synology_step_3: Install *KROMA* from the source; updates then arrive automatically.
download_family_nas_manual: Prefer a manual install? Download the `.spk` from the releases and go through Package Center → Manual Install.
download_closing_title: Signed for development, not for a store.
download_closing_body: The builds are signed with a development certificate, not a paid store certificate. That is the whole reason for the one-time setup per device (developer mode, quarantine, SmartScreen): once done, updates go through without friction. Everything stays self-hosted, your library and your activity never leave your network.
download_closing_note: A package that refuses to install? Most often a signature that changed: uninstall the old version, then reinstall.
privacy_head_description: What kroma.tv and the KROMA app do (and do not) collect: a static marketing site, self-hosted software, and the one service we operate, the push-notification relay.
privacy_intro: KROMA is free software that you host yourself, and kroma.tv is only a showcase. In short: this site collects almost nothing, and what the app does stays on your own hardware, on your own network.
privacy_card_description: Write to us with any question about this policy or about your data.
support_head_description: Where to get help with KROMA: by email, on GitHub, in the install guide and the docs. Plus how to report a bug well.
support_intro: KROMA is a free, self-hosted project. Depending on what you need, a question, a bug, an install to get going, here is the right door to knock on.
support_email_body: For anything that does not belong in a public issue, email is the most direct route. We read everything, and we reply in English as well as in French.
support_channel_issues_description: Report a bug or suggest a feature, in the same place as the code.
support_channel_install_description: Synology, Docker, Raspberry Pi, TV developer mode: the step-by-step install.
support_channel_docs_description: The repository, its per-component READMEs and the contributing notes.
support_bug_intro: A reproducible report is fixed far faster. Before opening an issue, gather the following if you can:
support_bug_item1: What you expected, and what actually happened.
support_bug_item2: The platform (web, Samsung Tizen, LG webOS, mobile, Apple TV / Android TV) and the version.
support_bug_item4: For a playback problem: the title's video codec (`hevc`, `h264` or `av1`) and audio (`ac3`, `eac3` or `aac`).
support_faq_a1: Yes. KROMA is free software under the GPL-2.0 license: free of charge, no subscription and no paid "pro" edition. The code is open, so you can audit it, modify it and redistribute it.
support_faq_a2: The web (desktop browser), mobile on iPhone / iPad / Android, Samsung (Tizen) and LG (webOS) televisions, as well as Apple TV and Android TV.
support_faq_q3: What do I need to self-host it?
